comparison: Both strongly support the fabrication methodology (C2, C19-C20, C31-C38, C40). OpenEval includes additional claims about FDTD simulations and experimental setup (C3, C21-C22, C41-C42, C44-C45) that peer reviewers address separately. All reviewers praise the novel fabrication approach as well-executed and convincing.

OpenEval R1 includes optical detection methodology claims (C3, C21-C22, C41-C42, C44-C45) that peer reviewers evaluate separately in R2. Peer R2 also includes methodological advantages (C95-C96) that OpenEval addresses in R5. Both recognize the optical detection as a key innovation.

Both strongly support the core diameter-dependent selectivity findings (C4, C23-C25, C46-C47, C50-C53, C55, C59-C60, C64-C66, C104-C108). OpenEval includes additional statistical analysis claims (C61-C62, C67) not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers. Peer R3 adds C114 about selectivity enhancement. Both emphasize the gradual nature of selectivity loss and consistency with prior work.

Both strongly support the CGMD simulation results and mechanistic insights (C5, C26-C27, C68-C72, C75-C82, C110-C113). OpenEval provides more detailed analysis of simulation methodology and void analysis. Peer reviewers confirm qualitative correlation with experimental data without raising methodological concerns.

Both support the Kap95 concentration effects and size-dependent modulation (C6, C28-C30, C86-C88, C90-C92, C94, C118, C120-C122). OpenEval explicitly notes uncertainty about biological relevance due to sub-physiological concentrations and high variability (C89, C93), while peer reviewers accept the findings without raising these concerns.

Both support methodological advantages of the optical detection system (C95-C96). OpenEval R5 also includes quantitative discrepancy discussions (C99-C103) that peer reviewers address in R9. OpenEval emphasizes order-of-magnitude improvement in detection efficiency.

Both support the transparent acknowledgment of quantitative discrepancies with theory and prior work (C99-C103). OpenEval presents these as part of methodological advantages discussion, while peer reviewers accept them as part of careful analysis without explicit concern.

Both support the FCS and lifetime measurements showing Kap95-Nsp1 interactions (C57-C58). OpenEval provides detailed interpretation about metal-induced fluorescence quenching, while peer reviewers accept these as part of comprehensive characterization without explicit discussion.

OpenEval R6 includes C56 (FCS measurements) that peer R8 addresses as a negative control result. Both accept this as part of the comprehensive experimental characterization, though peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss it.

Perfect agreement on acknowledgment of biomimetic system limitations compared to native NPCs (C97-C98). Both present these as honest limitations that do not undermine the validity of conclusions. Peer reviewers note the system as a valid starting point for future research.

Both address speculation about physiological NPC regulation (C115-C117). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature and gap between in vitro and cellular contexts, while peer reviewers SUPPORT the connection, with Reviewer 2 explicitly highlighting relevance to recent NPC dilation findings. OpenEval is more cautious about extrapolation to cellular function.

Both strongly support the literature background and context (C7-C18). OpenEval explicitly validates citations and identification of prior method limitations, while peer reviewers accept the background framework without question. Peer R12 also includes C1 (main research question) not in OpenEval R10.

OpenEval identifies experimental controls and corrections (C43, C48, C54) as important supported claims. These methodological details are not explicitly evaluated separately by peer reviewers, though they are part of the overall careful methodology that reviewers praise.

OpenEval separately evaluates comparisons with prior work and acknowledgment of sub-physiological Kap95 concentrations (C119, C123-C125). Peer reviewers do not separately address these claims, though they accept the overall Kap95 results and acknowledge the system's limitations.

Strong overlap on diameter-dependent selectivity claims. Peer R3 includes C114 (selectivity enhancement) that OpenEval addresses in R9. Both emphasize systematic measurements across multiple pores and gradual selectivity behavior.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R3 includes simulation claims C73-C74 (grafting density methodology) that peer R6 addresses as part of simulation validation. Both accept the simulation approach without methodological concerns.
